title: Nepal floods hit vulnerable communities as UNDP estimates 2.2 million tonnes of debris - United Nations Development Programme
description: Nepal floods hit vulnerable communities as UNDP estimates 2.2 million tonnes of debris  United Nations Development Programme
publisher.title: United Nations Development Programme
full_article:
Kathmandu/New York, 1 September 2026 – Floods and mudflows along Nepal’s Bhote Koshi–Trishuli river system have left at least 2.2 million tonnes of debris within the analysed areas, according to a preliminary estimate by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).

See the full RAPIDA (Rapid Assessment and Analysis) for Nepal.

The flash flood, reportedly triggered by a glacial collapse on 26 August, swept water, mud and rocks through communities in the affected districts. Nepal has reported over 1,000 dead, with over 4,000 people reported missing.

A total of 10,451 people has been rescued to date. 11 hydropower stations and one solar plant, totalling 431.1 megawatts, had stopped operating. Another 15 power projects under construction, with a planned capacity of 470 megawatts, were also damaged.

The floods have hit communities already facing hardship

The floods have struck communities that were already among the most vulnerable in Nepal. Around three in four affected people were living in areas where people already faced greater difficulties with their livelihoods, access to basic services and living conditions.

“This is a devastating disaster for communities along the Trishuli corridor. Families have lost loved ones, homes and livelihoods, while entire communities are struggling to reconnect with essential services and one another,” said Kyoko Yokosuka, UNDP Resident Representative in Nepal.

“The scale of destruction is immense, and as the immediate response continues, we must make sure that recovery reaches the people who have been hit hardest and helps them rebuild safely and with greater resilience,” she said.

Government figures show that 84,270 people have been affected across 17 municipalities in six districts. Most of the affected municipalities are rural and in Nepal’s hill regions, where 67.4% of people work in agriculture. For households dependent on agriculture, damage to crops, livestock and farmland could have a lasting impact on food security and family incomes. Nepal’s main monsoon planting season runs from June through September, making the timing of the floods particularly difficult for farming communities.

For this assessment , UNDP has combined satellite-based building damage assessments from Copernicus EMS and SERTIT with other available data and locally adapted engineering estimates to map the scale and location of debris. The preliminary findings will be updated as additional information becomes available.

RAPIDA is UNDP’s Rapid Assessment and Analysis for Immediate Recovery and Development Action methodology, which provides governments and partners with timely evidence to inform early recovery planning following disasters.

The debris includes parts of buildings, household belongings, vegetation, rocks and sediment. An estimated 556,200 tonnes comes from building debris, based on satellite assessments of damage covering 2,359 buildings. This figure is expected to rise as more damage is identified.

For families and rescue teams, the debris is more than a measure of the destruction: people remain trapped or missing beneath collapsed buildings and piles of mud and debris, making rescue operations difficult and dangerous.

The amount of debris shows the scale of the destruction and the challenge communities face as they clear homes, roads and public spaces and begin to rebuild. Damage to hydropower and other energy infrastructure has also disrupted electricity supplies, adding to the difficulties faced by communities and slowing the restoration of essential services.

translated:
काठमांडू/न्यूयॉर्क, १ सितम्बर २०२६ – संयुक्त राष्ट्र विकास कार्यक्रम (यूएनडीपी) केरऽ प्रारंभिक अनुमान के अनुसार नेपाल केरऽ भोटे कोशी–त्रिशुली नदी प्रणाली के साथ बाढ़ आरू कीचड़ के बहाव के वजह स॑ विश्लेषण करलऽ गेलऽ क्षेत्रऽ के भीतर कम स॑ कम २२ लाख टन मलबा छोड़लऽ गेलऽ छै ।

नेपाल के लिये सम्पूर्ण RAPIDA (Rapid Assessment and Analysis) देखें |

खबर छै कि 26 अगस्त क॑ हिमनदीय गिरला स॑ शुरू होय वाला ई आकस्मिक बाढ़ न॑ प्रभावित जिला केरऽ समुदायऽ के बीच स॑ पानी, कीचड़ आरू चट्टान क॑ बहाय देलकै । नेपालमे एक हजारसँ बेसी लोकक मृत्यु भेल अछि, जाहिमे ४ हजारसँ बेसी लोक लापता भेल अछि ।

आइ धरि कुल 10,451 लोक के बचाओल गेल अछि। 11टा जलविद्युत स्टेशन आ एकटा सौर संयंत्र, कुल 431.1 मेगावाट क परिचालन बंद भ गेल छल। निर्माणाधीन आओर 15 बिजली परियोजना, जेकर योजनाबद्ध क्षमता 470 मेगावाट अछि, सेहो नुकसान पहुंचल अछि।

बाढ़ि सं पहिने सं कठिनाई के सामना करय वाला समुदाय के नुकसान भेल अछि

बाढ़ि ओहि समुदाय पर आबि गेल अछि जे पहिने सँ नेपाल मे सबसँ बेसी कमजोर समुदाय मे सँ एक छल । चारि मे सं लगभग तीन प्रभावित लोक एहन इलाका मे रहैत छलाह जतय लोक के पहिने सं अपन रोजी-रोटी, बुनियादी सेवाक पहुंच आ जीवन-शैली मे बेसी दिक्कत के सामना करय पड़ैत छल.

नेपाल मे यूएनडीपी निवासी प्रतिनिधि क्योको योकोसुका कहलनि जे, त्रिशुली गलियारा के संग समुदाय के लेल ई एकटा विनाशकारी आपदा अछि, परिवार के अपन प्रियजन, घर आ रोजी-रोटी के नुकसान भेल अछि, जखन कि पूरा समुदाय आवश्यक सेवा आ एक दोसर सं फेर सं जुड़य लेल संघर्ष क रहल अछि।

हुनी कहलकै, “विनाश के पैमाना अपार छै, आरू जेना-जेना तत्काल प्रतिक्रिया जारी छै, हमरा ई सुनिश्चित करना चाहिय्यौ कि रिकवरी वू लोगऽ तलक पहुँचै जेकरा सबसें जादा नुकसान पहुँचलौ छै आरू ओकरा सुरक्षित आरू अधिक लचीलापन के साथ पुनर्निर्माण मँ मदद मिलै ।

सरकारी आंकड़ा बताबैत अछि जे छह जिलाक 17 नगरपालिका मे 84,270 लोक प्रभावित भेल अछि। अधिकांश प्रभावित नगरपालिका ग्रामीण आ नेपाल के पहाड़ी क्षेत्र मे अछि, जतय 67.4% लोक कृषि मे काज करैत छथि. कृषि पर निर्भर घरक कें लेल फसल, पशुधन आ खेती कें जमीन कें नुकसान कें खाद्य सुरक्षा आ परिवार कें आय पर स्थायी प्रभाव पड़य सकय छै. नेपाल केरऽ मुख्य मानसून रोपनी के मौसम जून स॑ सितंबर तलक चलै छै, जेकरा चलतें किसान समुदाय लेली बाढ़ केरऽ समय विशेष रूप स॑ मुश्किल होय जाय छै ।

अइ आकलन कें लेल यूएनडीपी न॑ कोपर्निकस ईएमएस आ सेर्टआईटी सं उपग्रह आधारित भवन क्षति आकलन कें अन्य उपलब्ध आंकड़ा आ स्थानीय रूप सं अनुकूलित इंजीनियरिंग अनुमानक कें साथ मिला क मलबा कें पैमाना आ स्थान कें नक्शा तैयार करलक छै. अतिरिक्त जानकारी उपलब्ध भेला पर प्रारंभिक निष्कर्ष कए अपडेट कएल जाएत।

रैपिडा यूएनडीपी कें तत्काल वसूली आ विकास कार्यवाही कें लेल तेजी सं आकलन आ विश्लेषण पद्धति छै, जे सरकारक आ भागीदारक कें आपदाक कें बाद शुरु आती रिकवरी योजना कें जानकारी देवय कें लेल समय पर सबूत उपलब्ध करायत छै.

मलबा मे भवन क किछु हिस्सा, घर क सामान, वनस्पति, चट्टान आ तलछट शामिल अछि। अनुमानित 556,200 टन भवन मलबा स॑ आबै छै, जे 2,359 भवनऽ क॑ कवर करै वाला नुकसान के उपग्रह आकलन के आधार प॑ छै । आओर नुकसान के पहचान भेला पर ई आंकड़ा बढ़य के उम्मीद अछि.

परिवार आरू बचाव टीम लेली ई मलबा तबाही केरऽ पैमाना स॑ भी जादा छै: लोग ढहलऽ भवन आरू कीचड़ आरू मलबा के ढेर के नीचें फंसलऽ या गायब होय जाय छै, जेकरा स॑ बचाव अभियान मुश्किल आरू खतरनाक होय जाय छै ।

मलबा केरऽ मात्रा विनाश केरऽ पैमाना आरू समुदायऽ क॑ सामने आबै वाला चुनौती क॑ दर्शाबै छै जब॑ वू घर, सड़क आरू सार्वजनिक जगहऽ क॑ साफ करी क॑ पुनर्निर्माण शुरू करी दै छै । जलविद्युत आ अन्य ऊर्जा बुनियादी ढाँचा कें नुकसान सं बिजली आपूर्ति मे सेहो बाधा पहुंचल छै, जे समुदायक कें सामने आवय वाला दिक्कतक कें बढ़ा रहल छै आ आवश्यक सेवाक कें बहाली मे धीमा भ गेल छै.

मीडिया सम्पर्क : १.

बॉन, जर्मनी: गैबी गोल्डमैन, संकट संचार प्रमुख: gabriela.goldman@undp.org

title: Nepal search operations continue a week after catastrophic floods - Al Jazeera
description: Nepal search operations continue a week after catastrophic floods  Al Jazeera
publisher.title: Al Jazeera
full_article:
A week on from devastating flash floods in the Himalayas that killed more than 1,100 people and left nearly 4,000 missing, search and rescue operations continue.

On August 26, a torrent of water, mud and rocks swept through communities in Nepal and China’s autonomous Tibet region after a glacial collapse, leaving behind a trail of destruction.

At least 1,114 people have been killed in Nepal, according to the Reuters news agency. In neighbouring Tibet, Chinese authorities have reported 16 deaths and 546 people missing.

The disaster left at least 2.2 million tonnes of debris, the United Nations Development Programme said, noting this was a preliminary estimate. The area affected in Nepal was home to 11 hydropower stations and one solar plant, which have stopped operating. Another 15 power projects under construction, with a planned capacity of 470 megawatts, were also damaged.

Al Jazeera’s Barnaby Lo, reporting from Kathmandu, says more specialised equipment is being flown in to help with search and rescue operations, especially for about 600 workers, some of whom are believed to be stuck in tunnels below the hydropower stations.

Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s office told Al Jazeera that more than 270 workers were rescued from the tunnel sites, not inside.

“Still, search and rescue operations are continuing. The Nepali army is drilling, digging and trying to reach those people. And pretty soon they are going to be joined by a team of foreign experts from South Korea after the arrival of Chinese and Indian experts who have been helping out for a few days now,” said Lo.

Advertisement

Forensic experts from China and Singapore are also due to arrive to help with the management and identification of the dead, which has become a daunting task given the mounting death toll and the state of the decomposing bodies.

“Families here have held funerals saying they need to do it even if they don’t have the bodies of their missing relatives to free their spirits,” Lo said.

In 2020, a UN-backed study (PDF) identified 47 potentially dangerous glacial lakes across Nepal, India and China.

Of those, 31 were placed in Rank I, the category considered to pose the highest risk of an outburst. The remaining lakes were classified as Rank II or III. Researchers called for closer monitoring of the lakes, early warning systems and other measures to reduce the risks to communities downstream.

The study also warned that rising temperatures were reshaping the Himalayan landscape. As glaciers retreat and fragment, new glacial lakes can form and existing ones can expand, increasing the risk of glacial lake outburst floods, or sudden releases of large volumes of water that can sweep through valleys downstream.

“These same experts are saying that it is becoming more dangerous and that the risk could be long-term, which means that people living in these villages might not be able to go back to rebuild their lives there,” Lo said.

In an interview with The Kathmandu Post, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal demanded compensation from large greenhouse gas emitters.

“Nepal’s greenhouse gas emissions are virtually negligible. Yet, we are paying the ultimate price for a global crisis we did not create. The rapid melting of glaciers and these catastrophic mountain tsunamis are direct consequences of global climate change,” Khanal said.

“The major industrial emitters – such as China, which is the world’s top emitter, the United States at number two, and India at number three – have a historical responsibility to compensate vulnerable nations like Nepal,” he said.

To this end, the country’s Ministry of Finance has officially dispatched a “formal climate compensation claim letter” to international partners, he added without specifying the names.
translated:
हिमालय म॑ विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ स॑ एक सप्ताह बाद जेकरा म॑ १,१०० स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलै आरू लगभग ४,००० लोगऽ के लापता होय गेलै, खोज आरू बचाव अभियान जारी छै ।

26 अगस्त क॑ हिमनदी केरऽ पतन के बाद नेपाल आरू चीन केरऽ स्वायत्त तिब्बत क्षेत्र केरऽ समुदायऽ म॑ पानी, कीचड़ आरू चट्टान केरऽ धार बहलै, जेकरा स॑ विनाश केरऽ निशान बनी गेलै ।

30 मे नेपाल-चीन बाढ़िक बाद फोटो सूची 2 of 3 नेपाल मे बाढ़ि सँ तबाह घर मे लोक घुरैत अछि

नेपाल मे बाढ़ि सं तबाह घर मे लोक वापसी करैत फंसल मजदूर के बचाबय लेल नेपाल के 3 दौड़ मे सं 3 के सूची दैत छथिन्ह, कारण बाढ़ मे मृतक के संख्या सूची के अंत मे 900 सं बेसि भ गेल अछि

नेपालमे १ हजार ११४ गोटेके मृत्यु भेल रायटर समाचार एजेन्सी जनौलक अछि । पड़ोसी देश तिब्बत मे चीन के अधिकारी 16 लोक के मौत आओर 546 लोक के लापता होय के खबरि देलक अछि.

संयुक्त राष्ट्र विकास कार्यक्रम न॑ कहलकै कि ई आपदा स॑ कम स॑ कम २२ लाख टन मलबा बनी गेलऽ छै आरू ई एगो प्रारंभिक अनुमान छै । नेपालमे प्रभावित क्षेत्रमे ११टा जलविद्युत् स्टेशन आ एकटा सौर संयंत्र रहल, जे परिचालन बंद कएने अछि । निर्माणाधीन आओर 15 बिजली परियोजना, जेकर योजनाबद्ध क्षमता 470 मेगावाट अछि, सेहो नुकसान पहुंचल अछि।

काठमांडू स॑ रिपोर्टिंग करतें हुअ॑ अल जजीरा केरऽ बरनाबी लो के कहना छै कि खोज आरू बचाव अभियान म॑ मदद लेली आरू विशेष उपकरण के उड़ान भरलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै, खास करी क॑ लगभग ६०० मजदूरऽ लेली, जेकरा म॑ स॑ कुछ मजदूर जलविद्युत स्टेशनऽ के नीचें सुरंगऽ म॑ फंसलऽ मानलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै ।

प्रधानमंत्री बलेन्द्र शाह केरऽ कार्यालय न॑ अल जजीरा क॑ बतैलकै कि सुरंग केरऽ जगहऽ स॑ २७० स॑ भी अधिक मजदूरऽ क॑ बचालऽ गेलै, अंदर नै ।

लो कहलनि जे, "तइयो खोज आ बचाव कार्य जारी अछि। नेपाली सेना ड्रिलिंग, खोदैत आ ओहि लोक तक पहुंचबाक प्रयास मे अछि। आ काफी जल्द चीनी आ भारतीय विशेषज्ञ के आगमन के बाद हुनका सब के संग दक्षिण कोरिया के विदेशी विशेषज्ञ के टीम सेहो शामिल होमय जा रहल अछि।"

विज्ञापन

चीन आरू सिंगापुर केरऽ फोरेंसिक विशेषज्ञ भी मृतकऽ के प्रबंधन आरू पहचान म॑ मदद करै लेली आबै वाला छै, जे बढ़तऽ मौतऽ के संख्या आरू सड़तऽ शवऽ के हालत क॑ देखत॑ हुअ॑ एगो कठिन काम बनी गेलऽ छै ।

लो कहलनि जे, एतय के परिवार अंतिम संस्कार केने अछि जे हुनका ई करय के जरूरत अछि भले हुनका लग अपन लापता रिश्तेदार के लाश नहि हो जे हुनकर मनोबल मुक्त भ सकय.

2020 म॑ संयुक्त राष्ट्र समर्थित एगो अध्ययन (पीडीएफ) न॑ पूरा नेपाल, भारत आरू चीन म॑ 47 संभावित खतरनाक हिमनदी झील के पहचान करलकै ।

ओहि मे स 31 कए रैंक I मे राखल गेल, जे श्रेणी मे फटकार क सबस बेसी जोखिम मानल गेल। शेष झील सब के रैंक II या III के रूप में वर्गीकृत करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । शोधकर्ता न॑ झीलऽ प॑ गहन निगरानी, ​​पूर्व चेतावनी प्रणाली आरू अन्य उपायऽ के आह्वान करल॑ छै ताकि नीचें के समुदायऽ लेली जोखिम क॑ कम करलऽ जाय सक॑ ।

title: ‘Pitiful’: experts condemn initial US aid contribution for Nepal flood victims - The Guardian
description: ‘Pitiful’: experts condemn initial US aid contribution for Nepal flood victims  The Guardian
publisher.title: The Guardian
full_article:
Aid experts have denounced the US’s “embarrassing” and “pitiful” initial response to the Nepal flood disaster after the US state department announced it was releasing $500,000 in emergency funds to help the relief effort.

The modest sum – which has since been increased – allocated in response to the devastation caused by mudslides in the mountainous Asian country was mocked on social media, where users contrasted it with the amount spent on other Trump administration priorities.

How the deadly Nepal and Tibet flash flood unfolded – a visual guide Read more

The death toll from last week’s flash floods has passed 1,000, with 4,400 people still unaccounted, according to officials in Nepal and China. Rescue teams are trying to find workers trapped in hydropower tunnels, which were buried in mud.

The US contribution has been upped to $3.6m, which state department officials say will be used to deliver food assistance to feed 10,000 affected households for up to three months, and pay for emergency items such as blankets, mosquito nets and shelter sheets.

However, seasoned humanitarian aid specialists suggest even that contribution is inadequate and say the US response has shrunk to a shadow of its previous capacity by the dismantling of USAID, the country’s main foreign assistance organization, after Donald Trump’s return to the White House last year.

The organization’s functions were taken over by the state department after USAID was terminated as an independent agency in July 2025 after being dismantled by the unofficial “department of government efficiency”, spearheaded by Elon Musk.

The state department says the US continues to support Nepal’s flood early warning system through grants.

However, foreign aid specialists highlighted the initial $500,000 sum as symbolic of the inadequacy of current US efforts compared to what would have been offered before USAID was dissolved. The state department has countered by saying it was “was designed to get immediate assistance moving while assessments were under way” and insisted the dismantling of USAID had “not slowed the US response”.

Mark Ward, a former head of USAID’s disaster response team, who was nicknamed “Mr Disaster” by President George HW Bush because of his prominent role in relief efforts, called the announcement “embarrassing for the United States and a bit of a slap at Nepal”.

Under USAID, Ward said, the amount would have been decided by a disaster assistance response team, which would have been on the ground immediately to assess needs because of the close working relationship the agency had with Nepal, a known natural disaster zone.

“They would have done an assessment very quickly with the Nepalese authorities, and then we would have decided on a number,” said Ward. “I’m sure it would have been a lot more than the figure that we’ve seen.”

His sentiments were echoed by George Ingram, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution and a former staff member of the House of Representatives foreign affairs committee.

“I was embarrassed for America,” he said. “It would have been better for them not to announce it.

“It’s too early to know what the total magnitude of the US assistance should be, but an initial offering of half a million dollars is pitiful. I do not recall a major disaster like this in which the US initial reaction was such a paltry amount.

“They should have said nothing focused on saying we need to figure out what the needs are.”

After news of floods broke last week, Karoline Leavitt, the outgoing White House press secretary, said the US embassy in Nepal was “in close contact with local authorities on the ground”.

“We’ve offered our help and assistance but of course, the first priority for this president and for Secretary Rubio will always be Americans,” she told Fox News. “We’re focused on rescuing every American that we possibly can.”

Ward, who worked on previous disasters in Nepal, said it was the country that the USAID had the closest relationship with because of its susceptibility to earthquakes and other natural catastrophes with humanitarian consequences.

“There was no country that we had a better relationship with than Nepal in their disaster management capacity, for the simple reason that nobody has more disasters than Nepal because of its topography,” he said. “We always had disaster experts there on our staff working with these guys, getting them ready for the next disaster, and they’re obviously gone now, with the dismantling of USAID.”

Current relief efforts are now being led by Nepal’s neighbors, India and China, said Ward, who argued that the US decision to skimp on foreign aid was a false economy.

“Is it really in the interest of the United States to have China and India in the lead?” he said. “The United States is safer when the world is more stable.

“If the world is unstable, there are more refugees trying to cross borders, and eventually, maybe ours. Maybe American troops have to deploy. So dealing with natural and man-made disasters before they get out of hand is in the interests of the United States, and it’s dirt cheap compared to the kinds of money you need to respond to a civil war, an insurrection or a refugee crisis.”

A state department spokesperson defended the US response as “fast, flexible, and driven by conditions on the ground – not arbitrary funding targets”.

“This is a needs-based, adaptive model that allows the United States to get assistance out the door immediately rather than delay action while waiting for a complete picture of a rapidly evolving disaster,” the spokesperson said. “The result is tangible assistance reaching affected Nepalis now.

“The United States is continuing to assess the situation and will adjust its response as circumstances warrant.”

अमेरिकी विदेश विभाग न॑ राहत प्रयास म॑ मदद लेली ५ लाख डॉलर के आपातकालीन कोष जारी करै के घोषणा के बाद नेपाल बाढ़ आपदा प॑ अमेरिका केरऽ “शर्मनाक” आरू “करुण” प्रारंभिक प्रतिक्रिया के निंदा करल॑ छै ।

पहाड़ी एशियाई देश मँ कीचड़ गिरला के कारण होय वाला तबाही के जवाब मँ आवंटित करलौ गेलौ मामूली रकम – जेकरा बाद मँ वृद्धि करलौ गेलौ छै – के सोशल मीडिया प मजाक उड़ाबै के कोशिश करलौ गेलौ छेलै, जहां यूजर्स नँ एकरौ विपरीत ट्रंप प्रशासन केरौ अन्य प्राथमिकता प खर्च करलौ गेलौ राशि के साथ बतैलकै ।

नेपाल आ तिब्बत के घातक फ्लैश फ्लड केना खुलल – एक दृश्य मार्गदर्शक Read more

नेपाल आ चीन के अधिकारी के अनुसार पिछला सप्ताह के आकस्मिक बाढ़ि सं मृतक के संख्या एक हजार सं आगू भ गेल अछि, जखन कि 4400 लोक के एखन धरि कोनो हिसाब नहिं अछि. बचाव दल जलविद्युत सुरंग मे फंसल मजदूर के खोजय के कोशिश मे अछि, जे थाल मे दबल छल.

अमेरिकी योगदान बढ़ा क॑ ३.६ मिलियन डॉलर करी देलऽ गेलऽ छै, जेकरऽ इस्तेमाल राज्य विभाग केरऽ अधिकारियऽ के कहना छै कि तीन महीना तलक १०,००० प्रभावित घरऽ क॑ पेट भरै लेली खाद्य सहायता पहुँचैलऽ जैतै, आरू आपातकालीन सामान जेना कि कंबल, मच्छरदानी आरू आश्रय चादर केरऽ भुगतान करलऽ जैतै ।

लेकिन अनुभवी मानवीय सहायता विशेषज्ञऽ के कहना छै कि योगदान अपर्याप्त छै आरू कहै छै कि पिछला साल डोनाल्ड ट्रंप केरऽ व्हाइट हाउस म॑ वापसी के बाद देश केरऽ मुख्य विदेशी सहायता संगठन यूएसएआईडी क॑ भंग करी क॑ अमेरिका केरऽ प्रतिक्रिया अपनऽ पिछला क्षमता के छाया म॑ सिकुड़ी गेलऽ छै ।

एलान मस्क केरऽ नेतृत्व म॑ अनौपचारिक “सरकारी दक्षता विभाग” द्वारा विघटन करला के बाद जुलाई २०२५ म॑ यूएसएआईडी क॑ स्वतंत्र एजेंसी के रूप म॑ समाप्त करला के बाद संगठन केरऽ काम क॑ राज्य विभाग न॑ संभाली लेल॑ छेलै ।

राज्य विभाग के कहनाय छनि जे अमेरिका अनुदान के माध्यम सं नेपाल के बाढ़ के पूर्व चेतावनी प्रणाली के समर्थन जारी रखने अछि.

लेकिन विदेशी सहायता विशेषज्ञ न॑ शुरुआती ५ लाख डॉलर केरऽ रकम क॑ यूएसएआईडी क॑ भंग करै स॑ पहल॑ जे पेशकश करलऽ जैतै, ओकरऽ तुलना म॑ मौजूदा अमेरिकी प्रयासऽ के अपर्याप्तता के प्रतीक के रूप म॑ रेखांकित करलकै । राज्य विभाग न॑ एकरऽ जवाब म॑ कहलकै कि एकरा “आकलन चलै के दौरान तत्काल सहायता क॑ आगू बढ़ाबै लेली डिजाइन करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै” आरू जोर देल॑ छै कि यूएसएआईडी क॑ भंग करै स॑ “अमेरिका केरऽ प्रतिक्रिया म॑ धीमा नै ऐलऽ छै” ।

यूएसएआईडी केरऽ आपदा प्रतिक्रिया टीम केरऽ पूर्व प्रमुख मार्क वार्ड, जेकरा राष्ट्रपति जॉर्ज एचडब्ल्यू बुश न॑ राहत प्रयास म॑ अपनऽ प्रमुख भूमिका के कारण “मिस्टर डिजास्टर” उपनाम देल॑ छेलै, न॑ ई घोषणा क॑ “अमेरिका लेली शर्मनाक आरू नेपाल प॑ कनी थप्पड़” बतैलकै ।

यूएसएआईडी के तहत ई राशि आपदा सहायता प्रतिक्रिया टीम द्वारा तय करलऽ जैतै, जे तुरंत जमीन प॑ आबी क॑ जरूरत के आकलन करतै, कैन्हेंकि एजेंसी केरऽ ज्ञात प्राकृतिक आपदा क्षेत्र नेपाल के साथ घनिष्ठ कामकाजी संबंध छेलै ।

वार्ड कहलनि जे, ओ सब नेपाली अधिकारी के संग बहुत जल्दी आकलन केने रहितथि, आ तखन हम सब एकटा नंबर के निर्णय लैत छलहुं। “हमरा यकीन अछि जे ई ओहि आंकड़ा स’ बहुत बेसी होइत जे हम सब देखलहुँ अछि.”

हुनकऽ भावना क॑ ब्रूकिंग्स इंस्टीट्यूशन केरऽ वरिष्ठ साथी आरू प्रतिनिधि सभा केरऽ विदेश मामलऽ के समिति केरऽ पूर्व कर्मचारी जॉर्ज इंग्राम न॑ भी गूंजलकै ।

ओ कहलनि जे, अमेरिका के लेल हम शर्मिंदा छलहुं। ओ कहला जे हुनका सब लेल नीक रहैत जे एकर घोषणा नहि करितथि।

“अमेरिका केरऽ सहायता केरऽ कुल परिमाण केतना होना चाहियऽ, ई जानना बहुत जल्दी छै, लेकिन डेढ़ लाख डॉलर केरऽ प्रारंभिक पेशकश करुण छै । हमरा एहि तरहक कोनो पैघ आपदा मोन नहि अछि जाहि मे अमेरिकाक प्रारंभिक प्रतिक्रिया एतेक क्षुद्र मात्रा मे छल ।

“हुनका सब के एहि बात पर केंद्रित किछु नहि कहबाक चाही छल जे हमरा सब के ई पता लगेबाक जरूरत अछि जे जरूरत की अछि।”

पिछला सप्ताह बाढ़ के खबर फटला के बाद व्हाइट हाउस के निवर्तमान प्रेस सचिव कैरोलिन लीविट के कहनाय छनि जे नेपाल मे अमेरिकी दूतावास “जमीन पर स्थानीय अधिकारी सं घनिष्ठ संपर्क मे अछि”.

फॉक्स न्यूज स॑ बातचीत म॑ हुनी कहलकै कि हम्में अपनऽ मदद आरू सहायता के पेशकश करल॑ छियै लेकिन निश्चित रूप स॑ ई राष्ट्रपति आरू सचिव रूबियो लेली पहलऽ प्राथमिकता हमेशा अमेरिकी ही होतै । “हम हर अमेरिकी के बचाबय पर ध्यान केंद्रित क’ रहल छी जे संभवतः हम क’ सकैत छी.”

नेपालमे पूर्व आपदा पर काज करनिहार वार्ड भूकम्प आ मानवीय परिणामक संग अन्य प्राकृतिक प्रलयके प्रति संवेदनशीलताक कारण यूएसएआईडीके सबसँ घनिष्ठ संबंध रहल बतौलनि ।

ओ कहलनि जे, कोनो एहन देश नहि छल जकर आपदा प्रबंधन क्षमता मे नेपाल स नीक संबंध छल, एकर सरल कारण अछि जे ओकर स्थलाकृति क कारण नेपाल स बेसी आपदा ककरो नहि अछि। “हमरा सबहक स्टाफ पर ओतय हमेशा आपदा विशेषज्ञ रहैत छल जे एहि लड़का सब के संग काज करैत छल, ओकरा सब के अगिला आपदा के लेल तैयार करैत छल, आ जाहिर अछि जे आब ओ सब चलि गेल अछि, यूएसएआईडी के विघटन के संग।”

वर्तमान राहत प्रयास के नेतृत्व आब नेपाल के पड़ोसी देश भारत आरू चीन करी रहलऽ छै, वार्ड न॑ कहलकै कि विदेशी सहायता म॑ कमी ​​करै के अमेरिका के फैसला झूठा अर्थव्यवस्था छेकै ।

“की सचमुच अमेरिका के हित में छै कि चीन आरू भारत के अगुवाई करलऽ जाय?” ओ कहलनि। ओ कहला जे अमेरिका तखन सुरक्षित रहैत अछि जखन दुनिया बेसी स्थिर रहैत अछि।

“जदि दुनिया अस्थिर छै त॑ सीमा पार करै के कोशिश म॑ शरणार्थी अधिक छै, आरू अंततः, शायद हमरऽ भी । शायद अमेरिकी सैनिक के तैनात करय पड़त. त’ प्राकृतिक आ मानव निर्मित आपदा के हाथ स’ निकलबा स’ पहिने ओकरा स’ निपटब अमेरिका के हित में अछि, आ गृहयुद्ध, विद्रोह या शरणार्थी संकट के जवाब देबय लेल जे तरहक पैसा चाही ओकर तुलना में ई गंदगी सस्ता अछि.”

प्रवक्ता नँ कहलकै, “ई जरूरत आधारित, अनुकूली मॉडल छै जेकरा स॑ अमेरिका क॑ तेजी स॑ विकसित होय रहलऽ आपदा केरऽ पूरा तस्वीर के इंतजार करतें हुअ॑ कार्रवाई म॑ देरी नै करी क॑ तुरंत दरवाजा स॑ बाहर मदद मिल॑ सकै छै । “परिणाम अखन प्रभावित नेपाली तक मूर्त सहयोग पहुँच रहल अछि ।

“अमेरिका स्थिति के आकलन जारी रखै छै आरू परिस्थिति के अनुसार अपनऽ प्रतिक्रिया में समायोजन करतै।”

full_article:
LONDON -- The death toll following the massive flash flooding along the Nepal-Tibet border climbed on Wednesday to 1,114 in Nepal, officials said, as the country's leader said his government would begin to shift its focus toward "rehabilitation."

The Nepali government's estimate for the missing remained at 3,916, the National Disaster Management Authority said in an update posted on social media at 9 a.m. local time.

People look at photographs of missing people on a wall outside Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital following the deadly flash floods and mudslide, reacts outside Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, in Kathmandu, Nepal, September 2, 2026. Athit Perawongmetha/Reuters

The U.S. State Department said on Tuesday it was tracking around 75 Americans who were unaccounted for across the Nepal-Tibet cross-border region. Fourteen Americans had made their way to safety, the department said.

Many more were recorded as injured in the week since the flooding destroyed towns and swept away structures, according to Nepali officials.

Prime Minister Balendra Shah of Nepal detailed on Tuesday the efforts his government was making to find those who were still missing, thanking local and international organizations for their "unprecedented courage, patience, support, cooperation and facilitation they have shown today."

"We are moving forward from search, rescue and relief distribution to rehabilitation after the devastating flood in the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa," Shah said in a social media post.

At least 1,114 bodies had been recovered in Nepal as of Wednesday morning, up from 1,003 a day earlier, disaster officials said in a post on social media.

Related Death toll tops 1,000 after Nepal flooding, as search continues for thousands

More than 21,000 security personnel from the national police, army and armed police forces have been dispatched to aid in search and rescue efforts, officials said.

"A team of Nepal Police including SOCO is conducting search and rescue operations in Timure, a flood-affected area in Rasuwa," the Nepal Police said in its own update, which was posted alongside images of flood victims in body bags and officers in protective clothing.

Relatives mourn during symbolic funerals held for flood victims still reported missing as they cremate Kush grass effigies in accordance with Nepali Hindu rites at Pashupatinath temple in Kathmandu on September 2, 2026. Prakash Mathema/AFP via Getty Images

The thousands of emergency responders had, as of Wednesday morning, doled out medical treatment to at least 4,070 people throughout several districts as of early Wednesday, officials said.

A state-affiliated media outlet in China, Xinhua News Agency earlier reported that Chinese officials said some 546 others were missing and 16 others were dead.

Shah, the Nepali prime minister, detailed on Tuesday the destruction throughout several regions in Nepal, saying that at least 48 suspension bridges had been damaged. Twenty-eight of those would have to be replaced altogether, he said.

A Nepal Army helicopter carries dead bodies from the flood affected area in Nepal's Rasuwa district on September 2, 2026. Prabin Ranabhat/AFP via Getty Images

Many more roads and villages and buildings were destroyed, he said, adding, "Details of the damaged physical infrastructure are being collected by helicopter and on foot."

The government released about 1 billion Nepali rupees, or about $6.5 million, to aid in the rebuilding of flood-affected areas, he said.

"This is not only the suffering of Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. It is a shared blow to the heart of the entire country," Shah told the country's legislators on Wednesday, according to The Kathmandu Post.

title: Smell of death hangs over rescue efforts in Nepal as deaths pass 1,100 - NBC News
description: Smell of death hangs over rescue efforts in Nepal as deaths pass 1,100  NBC News

full_article:
BIDUR, Nepal — At the Nepal army staging area in the heart of the flood zone, the roar of helicopters overhead carrying flood aid mixes with the rumble of a bulldozer digging a mass grave.

The overwhelming stench of death is crushing hopes that more survivors will be found in Bidur, a town in Nepal’s Nuwakot district, devastated by last week’s catastrophic floods.

Workers in white hazmat suits unload bodies from a stream of ambulances. They place the wrapped bodies onto a blue tarp in a cordoned-off area.

Helicopters, both military and private aircraft that in better days would be used for commercial tours, take off packed with aid before returning with survivors in need of medical care.

Kalpana Shrestha, a nurse who works in the capital, Kathmandu, is desperate. Ten members of her family are missing — her two sisters and their three children.

Kalpana Shrestha. Adam Galica / NBC News

A poster featuring Shrestha’s missing family members. Adam Galica / NBC News

“I have shared their photos with journalists, on social media and YouTube, but I have not got any response at all,” she told NBC News in Kathmandu on Tuesday. She added that her loved ones disappeared in Betrawati, a town some 60 miles from the capital that was obliterated in the flooding.

“I have posted so much that my fingers started shaking and trembling,” Shrestha, 35, said. “My mind has stopped working. But even so, we have not stopped posting.”

More than 1,114 have been declared dead in Nepal after last week’s devastating floods, according to Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority. Over 3,916 others are still missing, including at least 583 foreign nationals. In Tibet, at least 16 people were killed and 546 are missing, according to CGTN, China’s English-language satellite news channel.

A State Department spokesperson said Tuesday that 75 Americans remain unaccounted for and that 14 have made their way to safety in Nepal.

More than 10,000 people have been rescued so far, including 252 foreign nationals, the United Nations said.

The disaster, which was triggered by a glacier collapse and landslide on Nepal’s border with China, is now considered Nepal’s deadliest natural disaster since the April 2015 earthquake that killed around 9,000 people.

नेपालके राष्ट्रिय आपदा जोखिम न्यूनीकरण तथा प्रबन्धन प्राधिकरणके अनुसार विगत सप्ताहके विनाशकारी बाढिक बाद नेपालमे १ हजार ११४ स बेसीके मृत घोषित भेल अछि । 3916 स बेसी लोक एखनो लापता अछि, जाहि मे कम स कम 583 विदेशी नागरिक सेहो शामिल छथि। चीन केरऽ अंग्रेजी भाषा केरऽ सैटेलाइट न्यूज चैनल सीजीटीएन के अनुसार तिब्बत म॑ कम स॑ कम १६ लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलऽ छै आरू ५४६ लोगऽ के लापता छै ।

विदेश विभाग के प्रवक्ता मंगलदिन कहलनि जे, 75 अमेरिकी के हिसाब-किताब नहि अछि आ 14 गोटे नेपाल मे सुरक्षित स्थान पर पहुंच गेल छथि।

संयुक्त राष्ट्र जनौलक अछि जे एखन धरि १० हजार सँ बेसी लोक के बचाओल गेल अछि जाहि मे २५२ विदेशी नागरिक सेहो शामिल अछि ।

चीन के साथ नेपाल के सीमा पर ग्लेशियर के गिरला आरू भूस्खलन के वजह स॑ शुरू होय वाला ई आपदा क॑ अब॑ अप्रैल २०१५ केरऽ भूकंप के बाद नेपाल केरऽ सबस॑ घातक प्राकृतिक आपदा मानलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै जेकरा म॑ लगभग ९,००० लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलऽ छेलै ।

एम्हर, नेपालक जलविद्युत सुरंगक भीतर जीवित फँसल आशंका सँ दर्जनो मजदूर खोजबाक लेल नेपाली चालक दल आ विदेशी विशेषज्ञक दौड़ मे लागल अछि, तेँ त्वरित बचाव अभियानक आशा फीका पड़ि रहल अछि ।

नेपाल केरऽ स्वतंत्र बिजली उत्पादक संघ (इप्पन) के अनुसार सुदूर आरू पहाड़ी क्षेत्र केरऽ कई जिला स॑ गुजरै वाला त्रिशुली नदी के किनारे चलै वाला विभिन्न जलविद्युत परियोजना म॑ लगभग ९०० मजदूर लापता छै ।

ई साफ नै छै कि जब॑ पानी गिरलै त॑ वू मजदूरऽ म॑ स॑ कतेक लोग गहरा आरू भारी प्रबलित सुरंगऽ के भीतर छेलै । ई भी स्पष्ट नै छै कि ओकरा म॑ स॑ कतेक लोग अखनी भी जीवित होय सकै छै, जेकरा म॑ खराब मौसम, थाल, आरू सड़क आरू पुल जैसनऽ महत्वपूर्ण बुनियादी ढाँचा के नुकसान के कारण खोज आरू बचाव के प्रयास जटिल होय गेलऽ छै ।

खोज-बचाव के प्रयास में शामिल ब्रिगेडियर जनरल उजवाल राना बुधदिन कहलनि जे, सुरंग में थाल जेका तरल पदार्थ भरल रहैत अछि, दू-तीन दिन में ई काज पूरा करब संभव नहि अछि, स्थिति के देखैत हम देखैत छी जे तीन-चारि महीना में ई काज पूरा नहि भ सकैत अछि।

नेपाल-चीन मे बाढ़ि मे एक हजार सँ बेसी लोकक मृत्यु भेला सँ बचावकर्मी थाल आ मलबा मे कंघी करैत अछि

एम्हर, नेपालक प्रधानमन्त्री बलेन्द्र शाह कहलनि जे, सुरंग बचाव कार्य तखने प्रगति होयत जखन बाढ़ि सँ फेकल थाल सुखायत आ “स्थिर आधार स्थापित भ’ जायत”।

अधिकारी सब के अनुसार 1100 स बेसी लोक के जान गेल विनाशकारी बाढ़ि के बाद नेपाल आ चीन में बेहिसाब रहय वाला लगभग 4500 लोक में लापता जलविद्युत मजदूर शामिल अछि।

The arithmetic of climate injustice

And here is the arithmetic of the injustice: Nepal is one of the smallest contributors to global greenhouse gas emissions, yet its people, from remote villages to the Kathmandu Valley, keep paying the price for it. Nepal has grown its forest cover to nearly 46% of its land and draws around 90% of its electricity from clean hydropower. The climate disasters we face are the essence of climate injustice: those least responsible for the crisis are the first and worst affected, and too often the least equipped to recover.

full_article:
KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — Tourists previously reported missing in Nepal have made contact with authorities, officials said Wednesday, as families of locals still unaccounted for after last week’s catastrophic floods held symbolic funerals for their loved ones.

Nepal’s Foreign Ministry said 324 foreign nationals have been rescued, while another 590 from 39 countries remain missing following the Aug. 26 floods that killed at least 1,118 people and left more than 3,900 missing.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Wednesday that the number of Australians missing in the disaster had fallen from 43 to 38 after five were confirmed safe overnight.

“Amidst all of this tragedy, we are seeing some positive news. Today, another five Australians have been confirmed safe,” Albanese told reporters in Palau, where he is attending a regional summit.

Sunil Sharma, a spokesperson for the Nepal Tourism Board, said at least five other tourists who were previously reported missing had contacted authorities by email or telephone in recent days.

It is thought the disaster happened when a glacial collapse in the Himalayas sent rock, ice and meltwater into valleys below, triggering powerful floods downstream. The surge entered rivers flowing through Tibet and Nepal, causing them to rise rapidly. Floodwaters swept away homes, buildings, roads and bridges, carrying mud and rocks downstream.

Some families in Nuwakot, one of Nepal’s worst-affected districts, have held symbolic funerals for relatives still missing, hoping to free their souls after they were presumed dead.

In Hindu tradition, cremation is an important final rite, and for some families, performing the ceremony even without the bodies of their loved ones provides a sense of spiritual release.

Mukunda Rijal said his cousins and their daughters had not been found, prompting the family to perform a symbolic funeral for them.

Authorities in Nepal have also been burying recovered bodies in temporary graves until they can be identified. They are preserving DNA samples, photographing distinguishing facial features and recording other identifying details to help match the remains with missing people and eventually return them to their families.

China builds access road for rescue crews

On the Chinese side, rescue crews completed a makeshift road to the disaster site at Gyirong Port on the Nepal border, state broadcaster CCTV reported on Wednesday.

Crews have been clearing access for heavy machinery to be used in the search at the border crossing complex, which was washed away by the floods. The road leading to the crossing was destroyed and buried under water, mud and rocks.

At least 21 people have been killed and 541 remain missing in China, according to the Chinese state news agency Xinhua.

Survivors find shelter in Kathmandu

Some flood survivors are fleeing the devastation to seek shelter in Nepal’s capital, Kathmandu.

Around 400 survivors, mostly from the town of Timure, about 110 kilometers (65 miles) west of Kathmandu, have been staying at the Yellow Gumba monastery. The shelter is being organized by locals and relatives, with relief supplies donated by individuals and charity organizations.

Riya Tamang, 21, who fled with her 10-month-old baby as the floodwaters approached, is among those taking shelter at the monastery. She lost her grandparents in the disaster.

“I was the last one to leave the house. It was so difficult to escape,” she said.

Her husband, who works as a cook in Gyirong town on the Chinese side of the border, also survived, and the couple now stays in touch through video calls.

Helicopter pilot, Bibek Khadka, has told the BBC that families with missing loved ones due to Nepal's deadly flash floods have been reaching out to him for help.

Captain Khadka, who has previously worked in disaster rescue missions, has been scouring affected areas with his team to search for survivors, but he said he's found the balance between emotions and professionalism to be hard.

title: Nepal floods should mobilise climate action: UN green fund chief - France 24
description: Nepal floods should mobilise climate action: UN green fund chief  France 24
publisher.title: France 24
full_article:
Mafalda Duarte, executive director of the UN's multi-billion-dollar Green Climate Fund, said many countries do not understand the world faces tipping points from which it cannot go back.

"We see globally climate change dropping in terms of priorities, with other things -- conflicts and shocks -- taking priority," she told AFP.

"We see when there is will, that finance is mobilised to respond to emergencies. For some reason, we don't see the same type of response to climate -- as if we can afford to wait."

The Green Climate Fund was established by the UN to help developing countries deal with the impacts of climate change, and has invested $19 billion across 134 developing countries.

The US withdrew from the fund in January, and Britain halved its contribution in May.

The devastation caused by the Nepal flood disaster should return political focus to climate change, Duarte said.

"I would hope that this, plus the heatwaves this summer, plus the wildfires... These things are now happening everywhere. This is not a phenomenon of developing countries," she said, referencing the deadly fires and heatwave in across Europe.

Duarte is in Palau for the annual summit of Pacific island leaders, who see climate change as their biggest security threat.

Pacific governments reacted with dismay on Wednesday to a UN report that found the world would fail to limit global warming to 1.5C above pre-industrial levels, hastening climate impacts.

"It always surprises me as to how we can have so much information, and can act so little," she said.

"We cannot give up hope," she added.

The fund is increasing its work on adaptation in the Pacific, and has doubled its investment in the region in three years to $1 billion.

Acknowledging there is frustration among small countries accessing the fund, Duarte said the process has sped up to an average nine months.

Marshall Islands climate envoy Tina Stege, the Pacific's envoy for COP31, said on Wednesday that "urgent and concrete" progress was needed to improve access to climate finance for small island states.

She said a separate UN "loss and damage" fund, agreed four years ago to help developing nations respond to climate disasters, was "an empty bucket".

title: Nepal flood survivors cling to zipline to cross treacherous river - France 24
description: Nepal flood survivors cling to zipline to cross treacherous river  France 24
publisher.title: France 24
full_article:
The Nepal Army installed a roughly 250-metre (820-foot) temporary cable crossing in Bidur, offering a precarious lifeline across the river after devastating floods swept away roads and bridges.

Desperate people gathered on the riverbank, waiting for their turn to be hauled across.

Those needing urgent treatment, medicines, food and other essentials were ferried over the waters.

"My home was taken by the floods, and my family is in a shelter," said Sujan, 44, a chef from Amsterdam who returned to Nepal after the disaster struck on August 26, giving only one name.

Desperate people gathered on the riverbank, waiting for their turn to be hauled across © Arun SANKAR / AFP

Unable to secure a helicopter, he came to the river crossing hoping to reach his wife, two children and elderly mother.

The catastrophic flooding has killed more than 1,200 people and left nearly 4,800 missing in Nepal and China's Tibet region.

Rescuers are still searching for survivors and victims, with helicopters flying food, temporary shelters and medicine to those left with almost nothing.

Devi Maji, 31, arrived at the zipline with her three-year-old son after becoming stranded in Trishuli.

"I want to get back to my village to see my husband and my other two children," said the daily wage worker.

Rescuers are still searching for survivors and victims, with helicopters flying food, temporary shelters and medicine to those left with almost nothing © Arun SANKAR / AFP

For Bhishma Bhatta, 40, there was no time to wait.

His mother Tulkumaari developed severe breathing difficulties overnight, and the family ran out of oxygen.

"We somehow managed to get her on the zipline... and take her to hospital," he said.

The army said the crossing was the first of five temporary cable links planned along the flood-hit Trishuli River.

title: Did Climate Change Cause the Flooding in Nepal? - Rolling Stone
description: Did Climate Change Cause the Flooding in Nepal?  Rolling Stone
publisher.title: Rolling Stone
full_article:
A flash flood that struck Nepal last week has left over 1,000 people dead, and thousands more are missing. A landslide that was first thought to be the result of an earthquake actually looks to have resulted from a confluence of events surrounding part of a glacier breaking free at a high altitude, along with the loose earth surrounding it. Researchers around the world are using satellite imagery to try to understand what happened.

Video of the flood quickly spread online, though some had been fabricated by AI. Legitimate footage showed torrents of water sweeping through a valley. After the satellite data was initially analyzed, it was determined that part of a glacier in the mountains had snapped off, and the ice had melted as it cascaded downward and caused this flood. Essentially, there was an ice avalanche. A powerful mixture of rock, earth, and water plunged through the valleys of the Himalayas and made its way to populated areas.

The story is a little more complicated than that, though, according to experts who study these kinds of glaciers. Daniel Shugar, a geologist at the University of Calgary in Canada, tells Rolling Stone that much more than that piece of glacier broke off the mountain.

“A giant chunk of the mountainside — we don’t know the exact volume yet — broke loose and took a piece of the glacier with it,” Shugar says.

It may be that warm temperatures thawed permafrost on the mountain, allowing meltwater to seep into rock fractures and loosen the mountainside, which caused this disaster. This permafrost essentially holds together the mountainside near these glaciers. If that becomes structurally unsound, it can take part of the glacier with it, as the satellite images appear to show.

“A couple dozen other scientists are working on this [research] together, around the world,” Shugar says, noting that there’s a Slack channel where they share satellite images and observations. “It’s a global community of scientists volunteering our time, expertise, and skills to cooperate on figuring this out.”

Marin Clark, a geophysicist at the University of Michigan, says the material that made up the landslide was traveling incredibly fast down the mountain. The friction from the speed could quickly melt the ice within it — as well as ice it came in contact with as it slid — which could have contributed to the immense floodwaters.

“It reached the first affected town in only seven minutes,” Clark says. “We have a lot of trouble attributing any one specific event to climate change. But what we do know is that the warming conditions we’ve seen in Himalaya over the last several years are exactly the kind that can lead to processes like what we observed last week.”

Clark says large, sediment-laden floods in this region have been increasing in number over the last decade or so, and warming temperatures appear to be part of the cause. Nepal itself is blaming climate change for what happened here, as it is applying for $5 billion in aid from the United Nations climate fund.

Shugar notes that changes in the weather could have contributed to the conditions that caused this flood, not just the melting of permafrost.

“If you change the seasonality of precipitation — more rain instead of snow, or more winter rain than there used to be — that can lead to slope stability issues, too,” Shugar says. The more liquid water is present on the ground, the more unstable it is.

This event is analogous to one geologists observed in 2021, known as the Chamoli disaster in India. That catastrophic flash flood looks to have been caused by melting permafrost and increased rainfall, as well as retreating glaciers, in a high-altitude region. “This is a similar kind of thing, where you have this flood downstream and nobody initially knew what it was or what caused it,” Shugar says. “People thought it must be a glacial lake outburst flood, but it was a landslide with a piece of glacier on top that collapsed and melted all of the ice.” Trending Stories Sean Ono Lennon Confirms Birth of Baby Boy, John Lennon and Yoko Ono's First Grandchild Alanis Morissette Sues Former Tour Manager, Alleges ‘Extortionate’ Threat Over Airport Drugs Jonathan Bailey Drops Out of West End Musical After Ariana Grande’s Departure Lizzo Scores Court Win as Judge Tosses Tour Staffer’s Harassment, Discrimination Lawsuit

How exactly climate change played a role in the flood remains to be seen, but there are many indicators pointing to human impacts on the climate being a major factor. Clark says that because these types of events are becoming more common, early warning is going to be crucial for these types of regions, such as sending out alerts when seismic activity is detected.

“Early warning is probably the highest priority — developing systems that recognize the seismic signals that may be the initial trigger, giving communities downstream enough time to evacuate to higher ground and enough time for workers to get out of tunnels,” Clark says.

बाढ़िक वीडियो जल्दीए ऑनलाइन पसरल, हालांकि किछु एआई द्वारा गढ़ल गेल छल। वैध फुटेज मे एकटा घाटी मे पानिक धार बहैत देखाउल गेल। उपग्रह केरऽ आंकड़ऽ के शुरूआत म॑ विश्लेषण के बाद ई तय करलऽ गेलै कि पहाड़ऽ म॑ एगो ग्लेशियर केरऽ कुछ हिस्सा टूटी गेलऽ छै, आरू नीचें के तरफ झरना के साथ बर्फ पिघली गेलऽ छै आरू ई बाढ़ के कारण बनलऽ छै । अनिवार्य रूप स बर्फक हिमस्खलन भेल। हिमालय के घाटी में चट्टान, धरती आ पानिक एकटा शक्तिशाली मिश्रण डूबि क आबादी वाला इलाका में अपन जगह बना लेलक |

कथा एहि सं कनि बेसी जटिल अछि, तथापि, एहि तरहक ग्लेशियरक अध्ययन करयवला विशेषज्ञ लोकनिक अनुसार. कनाडा केरऽ कैलगरी विश्वविद्यालय केरऽ भूवैज्ञानिक डेनियल शुगर रोलिंग स्टोन क॑ बतैलकै कि ग्लेशियर केरऽ वू टुकड़ा स॑ भी बहुत अधिक पहाड़ स॑ टूटी गेलै ।

मिशिगन विश्वविद्यालय केरऽ भूभौतिकी विज्ञानी मरीन क्लार्क के कहना छै कि भूस्खलन केरऽ निर्माण करै वाला सामग्री पहाड़ स॑ नीचें अविश्वसनीय रूप स॑ तेजी स॑ जाय रहलऽ छेलै । गति स॑ निकलै वाला घर्षण ओकरा भीतर के बर्फ क॑ जल्दी पिघला सकै छेलै — साथ ही साथ फिसलतें-फिसलतें ओकरऽ संपर्क म॑ आबै वाला बर्फ भी — जेकरा स॑ अपार बाढ़ के पानी म॑ योगदान मिल॑ सकै छेलै ।

क्लार्क कहैत छथि जे इ मात्र सात मिनट मे पहिल प्रभावित शहर मे पहुंच गेल। "हमरा सब क॑ कोनो भी एगो विशिष्ट घटना क॑ जलवायु परिवर्तन के कारण बताबै म॑ बहुत परेशानी होय छै ।लेकिन हमरा सब क॑ जे पता छै कि पिछला कई साल स॑ हिमालय म॑ जे वार्मिंग केरऽ स्थिति हम्मं॑ देखै छियै, वू ठीक वैन्हऽ तरह के छै जेकरा स॑ ऐसनऽ प्रक्रिया पैदा होय सकै छै जेना कि हम्मं॑ पिछला सप्ताह देखलियै।”

क्लार्क के कहना छै कि पिछला एक दशक या एकरा स॑ भी अधिक समय स॑ ई क्षेत्र म॑ बड़ऽ, तलछट स॑ भरलऽ बाढ़ के संख्या बढ़ी रहलऽ छै आरू तापमान म॑ गर्मी बढ़ना एकरऽ कारण के हिस्सा प्रतीत होय रहलऽ छै । एतय जे किछु भेल ताहि लेल नेपाल स्वयं जलवायु परिवर्तन केँ जिम्मेदार ठहरा रहल अछि, कारण ओ संयुक्त राष्ट्र जलवायु कोष सँ ५ अरब डॉलर केर सहायता लेल आवेदन क’ रहल अछि ।

शुगर नोट करै छै कि मौसम में बदलाव के कारण ई बाढ़ के कारण बनलऽ परिस्थिति में योगदान हो सकै छेलै, खाली परमाफ्रॉस्ट के पिघलना नै ।

शुगर कहै छै, “जदि आपने वर्षा के मौसमीपन बदलै छियै - बर्फ के जगह अधिक बारिश, या जाड़ा के समय पहलें स॑ अधिक बारिश - त॑ ढलान के स्थिरता के मुद्दा भी पैदा होय सकै छै । जमीन पर जतेक तरल पानि रहैत अछि, ओतेक अस्थिर रहैत अछि ।

ई घटना २०२१ म॑ भूवैज्ञानिकऽ द्वारा देखलऽ गेलऽ एगो घटना के अनुरूप छै, जेकरा भारत म॑ चमोली आपदा के नाम स॑ जानलऽ जाय छै । ओ विनाशकारी फ्लैश फ्लड केरऽ कारण लगै छै कि ई पर्माफ्रॉस्ट केरऽ पिघलना आरू बढ़लऽ बारिश के साथ-साथ पीछे हटै वाला ग्लेशियर केरऽ कारण उच्च ऊंचाई वाला क्षेत्र में होय छै । संबंधित सामग्री अक्षय ऊर्जा चुनाव पर पैघ खर्च करय लागल अछि. ई काज क’ रहल अछि, बहुत आदिवासी कार्यकर्ता हमर ग्रह के बचाबय के कोशिश क’ रहल छथि. हमरा सब के सुनय पड़त लियो एआई पर ल’ क’ ओ ग्रह के पोप देखाबैत छथि एहि आश्चर्यजनक जलवायु जीत के अनदेखी नहि करू

शुगर कहैत छथि, “ई सेहो एहने तरहक बात अछि, जतय अहाँक ई बाढ़ि नीचाँ अछि आ शुरू मे ककरो नहि बुझल छल जे ई की अछि आ एकर कारण की अछि।” “लोक सब सोचलकै कि ई हिमनदी झील केरऽ फटला के बाढ़ होतै, लेकिन ई भूस्खलन छेलै जेकरऽ ऊपर ग्लेशियर केरऽ टुकड़ा छेलै जे ढह गेलै आरू सब बर्फ पिघली गेलै।” ट्रेंडिंग स्टोरीज शॉन ओनो लेनन न॑ बेबी बॉय केरऽ जन्म के पुष्टि करलकै, जॉन लेनन आरू योको ओनो केरऽ पहलऽ पोता अलनिस मोरिसेट न॑ पूर्व टूर मैनेजर प॑ मुकदमा करलकै, हवाई अड्डा प॑ ड्रग्स प॑ ‘उत्पीड़न’ के धमकी के आरोप लगैलकै जोनाथन बेली न॑ एरियाना ग्रांडे केरऽ प्रस्थान के बाद वेस्ट एंड म्यूजिकल स॑ बाहर निकली गेलै लिज्जो न॑ कोर्ट जीत के स्कोर करलकै जब॑ जज न॑ टूर स्टाफ केरऽ परेशानी, भेदभाव टॉस करलकै मुकदमा

बाढ़ म॑ जलवायु परिवर्तन न॑ ठीक-ठीक केना भूमिका निभैलकै, ई देखना छै, लेकिन जलवायु प॑ मानवीय प्रभाव क॑ एकरऽ प्रमुख कारक के रूप म॑ इशारा करै वाला बहुत सारा संकेतक छै । क्लार्क के कहना छै कि ई तरह के घटना आम होय रहलऽ छै, ई लेली ई तरह के क्षेत्रऽ लेली जल्दी चेतावनी देना बहुत महत्वपूर्ण होय वाला छै, जेना कि भूकंपीय गतिविधि के पता चलला प॑ अलर्ट भेजना ।

क्लार्क कहै छै, “जल्दी चेतावनी संभवतः सबस॑ अधिक प्राथमिकता छै — ऐन्हऽ प्रणाली विकसित करना जे भूकंपीय संकेत क॑ पहचानै छै जे प्रारंभिक ट्रिगर होय सकै छै, जेकरा स॑ नीचे के समुदाय क॑ उच्च जमीन प॑ खाली करै लेली पर्याप्त समय मिल॑ सक॑ आरू मजदूरऽ क॑ सुरंगऽ स॑ बाहर निकलै लेली पर्याप्त समय मिल॑ सक॑ ।
